$schema_note: STRUCTURE ONLY. Which pipeline module owns which stage, and which module is whose parent. Generated from `modules` and `stages` in PostgreSQL -- see app/module_split.py::split_config. It no longer decides where a field goes: since Round 7 that is field_placements, and spec/fields.json is generated from it already placed. The blocks that used to describe field placement (`own`, `shared`, `read_through.fields`, `relocated_fields`, `section_order`) were removed so this file cannot be mistaken for a second authority. src/lib/spec/moduleSplit.ts reads only the blocks below.

ranges.$note: Inclusive stage bounds. applies_to in spec/stages.json is now WRONG - it still says stages 4 to 7 are 'lead'. It is ignored, and a register-correction row on the Spec Health page asks for the workbook to be regenerated. Nothing reads applies_to any more.

stage_field.$note: The field each module stores its own stage in. Deals keeps the register's deal_stage rather than gaining project_stage. Read by the progression resolver and by stageOptionsFor().

stage_options.$note: Stage options are DERIVED from the range above plus spec/stages.json, never from a picklist. That is deliberate and it closes three register problems at once rather than papering over them in a sidecar: leads_stage still carries dead 4_RFP_RFI..7_CLOSE keys, deals__deal_stage has no 7_CLOSE at all (so a Deal opening at Stage 7 would have nothing to store), and stages.json.applies_to disagrees with this file. All three are raised as register corrections on the Spec Health page. NO PICKLIST ENTRIES ARE ADDED HERE.

reassign.$note: Reassignment by capture stage, off the Leads sheet. A field follows the stage that captures it. 53 fields move: 45 to Opportunities, 8 to Deals. Every ref that named one of them as leads.<api_name> keeps resolving through the loader's movedRefs fall-through - see src/lib/spec/moduleSplit.ts.

read_through.$note: Identity. These are READ THROUGH THE PARENT and rendered read-only - never copied, so the same value cannot drift in two places. They must appear in fieldsOf(module) even though the record does not store them: compileFor() checks every identifier in a computed_expr, a visibility_condition and a condition against the module's api_name set, so a criterion or formula naming a parent field would otherwise stop compiling. sub_segment removed and country, theme, lighthouse_project, gorilla_flag added at the Country/Theme/ROB-gap pass — see spec/extensions.json open_questions. country, city_state, destination_region and booking_region added at the geography pass (02 Sep 2026): region was already read-through, and geography is identity of the pursuit - copying it onto the Opportunity and again onto the Deal is the two-places-to-drift bug this mechanism exists to prevent. region REMOVED at the geography pass follow-up (02 Sep 2026): leads.region was retired from the register in favour of destination_region and booking_region, so there is no parent field left to read through.

register_corrections.detail: applies_to still says stages 4, 5, 6 and 7 are 'lead'. Under the split, 4-6 belong to Opportunities and 7 to Deals. Nothing reads applies_to any more - spec/module_split.json ranges are the authority - but the workbook should be regenerated so the two agree.

Still carries 4_RFP_RFI, 5_TECHNICAL_EVAL, 6_COMMERCIAL_EVAL and 7_CLOSE. A Lead now stops at Stage 3, so four of its eight keys are unreachable from the Leads module. Stage options are derived from the module range instead of this picklist; regenerate it from the split.

Carries 8_PROJECT_SUCCESS, 9_EXPANSION and CLOSED. A Deal now OPENS at Stage 7 and there is no 7_CLOSE key to store. Stage options are derived from the module range instead. Separately, CLOSED is a status, not a stage, and does not belong in a stage picklist.

The Deals sheet names the record's creation timestamp created_by_date and its modification timestamp modified_by_date, where every other sheet uses created_date / modified_date plus a separate created_by lookup. The shared SYSTEM section therefore lands a near-duplicate pair on Deals. Declared in shared.equivalence above; rename in the workbook rather than in a sidecar.

The Deals sheet names the record's creation timestamp created_by_date and its modification timestamp modified_by_date, where every other sheet uses created_date / modified_date plus a separate created_by lookup. The SYSTEM section is placed on all three pipeline modules, so Deals ends up with a near-duplicate pair: leads.created_date and deals.created_by_date are the same concept under two names, as are leads.modified_date and deals.modified_by_date. NOT collapsed -- dropping either row would hide the inconsistency behind a loader. Rename in the workbook. (Previously declared in this file's `shared.equivalence` block, which Round 7 removed along with the rest of the placement blocks.)

register_corrections.ref: leads.payment_milestones and its four milestone row-columns
register_corrections.detail: The register captures payment_milestones at Stage 7; this build places it at Stage 6 -- payment milestones are the payment SCHEDULE and belong to the commercial terms negotiated during Commercial Evaluation, not to the paperwork closed out afterwards. It therefore renders on Opportunities, not Deals, and its four row columns (milestone planned / actual / invoice / payment received date) travel with it. A deliberate product decision, not a register defect. It used to be an override in this file's `relocated_fields` block; since Round 7 the placement simply HAS capture_stage 6 and there is nothing to override, so it is recorded here instead. Confirm the register should be corrected to match.
